title: Updates on Unemployment and Retrenchment Numbers and Adoption of Schemes such as SGUnited Traineeships
what_it_is: Updates on Unemployment and Retrenchment Numbers and Adoption of Schemes such as SGUnited Traineeships

sections.label: Retrenchment, unpaid leave, traineeship misuse
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Manpower about retrenched Singaporeans, unpaid leave, pay cuts, and misuse of traineeship programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower how many Singaporeans have (i) been retrenched this year (ii) been placed on unpaid leave due to the COVID-19 situation and (iii) had their pay reduced by more than 50% since the start of the circuit breaker period.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is being done to ensure that companies do not misuse the SGUnited Traineeships Programme and SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programme to fulfil their manpower requirements; and (b) whether companies that have recently retrenched their workers are allowed to hire under the these traineeship programmes.

sections.label: Unemployed residents second quarter 2020
sections.summary: The Advance Release estimated 90,500 unemployed residents in June 2020, compared to 73,900 in December 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Advance Release for the second quarter of 2020 estimated that there were 90,500 unemployed residents in June 2020, compared to 73,900 in December 2019.

sections.label: Singapore Citizens retrenched first half 2020
sections.summary: Preliminary survey data indicate 5,280 Singapore Citizens were retrenched in the first half of 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To Ms He Ting Ru’s question, preliminary figures from the survey data indicate that 5,280 Singapore Citizens were retrenched in the first half of 2020.

sections.label: Opportunities made available
sections.summary: More than 95,000 opportunities were made available, including 65,000 jobs, close to 20,000 company-hosted places, and over 10,000 SGUnited Skills places.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: By now, more than 95,000 opportunities have been made available.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: These include: (a) 65,000 job opportunities, (b) close to 20,000 company-hosted traineeships, attachments or training places, and (c) over 10,000 opportunities under the SGUnited Skills Programme.

sections.label: Jobs Growth Incentive scheme
sections.summary: The new Jobs Growth Incentive scheme will give greater support to businesses to expand and grow their local headcounts over the next six months.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The new Jobs Growth Incentive scheme will give greater support to businesses to expand and grow their local headcounts over the next six months.

sections.label: Wage subsidies for local hires
sections.summary: New local hires aged 40 and above attract twice as much wage subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: New local hires aged 40 and above attract twice as much wage subsidies.

sections.label: Rejecting trainee replacement applications
sections.summary: Applications will be rejected if there are grounds to believe companies are replacing existing employees with trainees in similar roles.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If there are grounds to believe that companies are replacing existing employees with trainees in similar roles, such applications will be rejected.

sections.label: Host companies monthly updates to SBF
sections.summary: Host companies for traineeships must submit monthly updates to SBF on what is happening to the traineeship.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The host companies for the traineeships have to submit monthly updates to SBF as to what is happening to the traineeship.

sections.label: More frequent unemployment data reliability
sections.summary: Unemployment data is quarterly and is being looked at for monthly provision if reliable enough for decision-making.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We are looking at one of the statistics that we can provide at a more regular interval – today, it is available on a quarterly basis.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We are looking at whether unemployment data can be reliably provided on, perhaps, a monthly basis.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It has to do with whether it is reliable and you can count on it for decision-making.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And if it is not reliable because the data-set is not going to be large enough, then by providing even more granular data at even closer intervals does not necessarily help in decision-making.

sections.label: Protecting whistle blowers and outreach
sections.summary: Efforts will be made to protect whistle blowers' identity and expand outreach so people can raise issues safely.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I can appreciate that in some instances if the persons, for example, are still employed by the company, they are very careful and want to make sure that they do not get identified as the whistle blower.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We are very mindful of that and we will make all effort to protect their identity.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To expanding the outreach to encourage, individuals to step forward, I agree with her, entirely, especially for workers who are likely to be more vulnerable and less able to appreciate how best they can advance their interests.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We educate them, not just on the ground, but also through the use of the vernacular media.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will have to continue to step up these efforts and ensure that people feel the sense that they can raise these issues safely.
